Added the `params` MAP<STRING, STRING> column to the Parquet writer in the flusher for full Iceberg schema compatibility.

## Changes Made
- Added `MapArray` and `OffsetBuffer` imports for map type support
- Implemented columnar map array construction for the `params` field
- Added `params` field to Arrow schema with `DataType::Map`
- Included `params_array` in the RecordBatch output

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** The existing columnar Parquet writer infrastructure was well-designed; adding the params map was straightforward by following the same pattern as other fields.
- **What didn't:** N/A - implementation worked on first attempt.
- **Surprise:** The Arrow MapArray API requires building offsets manually and wrapping values in a StructArray - more verbose than simple array types.
- **Reusable pattern:** For adding map columns to Parquet in Arrow: build key/value vectors, compute offsets, create StructArray, wrap in MapArray with proper field definition.

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md §Phase 2 L154-159 — "Deployment: Target ardenone-manager
cluster; Services: Collector + Flusher deployments; Persistent volume for shared logs".

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
All three pods have been Pending for 56 days and can never schedule:

    kubectl -n trace get pods
      trace-collector-776fc78684-2bbgl  0/1 Pending  56d
      trace-collector-776fc78684-wls2c  0/1 Pending  56d
      trace-flusher-6d6bc686dc-t7hfs    0/1 Pending  56d

    describe -> FailedScheduling (x4086 over 14d):
      "0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims"

    kubectl -n trace get pvc
      trace-dlq   Pending  nfs-client  56d
      trace-logs  Pending  nfs-client  56d

Root cause: both PVCs request storageClassName "nfs-client", which does not exist on
this cluster. The only classes available are:
      local-path (default)  rancher.io/local-path            WaitForFirstConsumer
      nfs-synology          ...synology-nfs...provisioner    Immediate

Set in declarative-config/k8s/ardenone-manager/trace/pvc.yaml:14 (50Gi) and
dlq-pvc.yaml:14 (5Gi).

The fix is a declarative-config commit -> ArgoCD sync. Do NOT kubectl patch the PVCs;
a PVC's storageClassName is immutable anyway, so the existing two must be deleted and
recreated by ArgoCD after the manifest change -- confirm nothing on them is worth
keeping first (they never bound, so they hold no data).

Choose nfs-synology (Immediate binding, ReadWriteMany-capable, matches the "shared
logs" intent) unless a reason to prefer local-path is recorded in the commit message.

## Done when
    kubectl --server=http://traefik-ardenone-manager:8001 get pvc -n trace
-> both trace-dlq and trace-logs show STATUS Bound

    kubectl --server=http://traefik-ardenone-manager:8001 get pods -n trace
-> trace-collector and trace-flusher pods are Running, 1/1 Ready
issue.title: Point the trace PVCs at a storage class that exists on ardenone-manager

Completed core analytics query library for three primary metrics.

Created three DuckDB query files in analytics/queries/:

1. **core_ctr.sql** (4414 bytes) - CTR by campaign/ad/creative
   - CTR by campaign with network breakdown
   - CTR by creative (headline + image combinations)
   - Daily CTR trends by network
   - Campaign x Creative matrix for fatigue analysis

2. **core_dwell_time.sql** (7940 bytes) - Aggregate heartbeat pings into time-on-page
   - Dwell time by session using explicit dwell events
   - Dwell time by landing page (aggregated)
   - Dwell time by campaign/creative for performance correlation
   - Inferred dwell time from event sequences (for sessions without explicit dwell events)
   - Dwell time distribution histogram

3. **core_funnel.sql** (12281 bytes) - Session chain from ad click to conversion
   - Full funnel analysis by campaign (impression → click → engagement → conversion)
   - Funnel by creative (headline + image performance)
   - Drop-off analysis identifying where users abandon
   - Time-to-convert analysis
   - Daily funnel trend monitoring

- **What worked:** Leveraged existing schema files (sessions_iceberg.sql, ad_events_iceberg.sql) to understand the data model before writing queries. The template format used by existing queries (campaign_funnel.sql, ctr_by_campaign.sql) provided a consistent pattern.
- **What didn't:** Initially considered using raw event sequences for dwell time, but realized the schema includes explicit dwell_time_ms and dwell_visible_pct fields from V003 migration, making queries more accurate.
- **Surprise:** The schema already has comprehensive engagement metrics (scroll_depth_pct, scroll_time_ms, dwell_time_ms, dwell_visible_pct) added in V003, reducing the need for complex inference logic.
- **Reusable pattern:** Core analytics queries should be organized by metric type (CTR, dwell time, funnel) with multiple variants per file (by dimension, aggregated, trends) for comprehensive coverage.

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md §Phase 2 "CI/CD & Deployment" names Collector CI and Flusher
CI as the templates that exist. Phases 4/5/8 then ship syncer, compactor and analytics
as first-class components -- with no CI to build them.

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
The repo carries five templates under .argo/:
    trace-analytics-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml    <- repo only
    trace-collector-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml    <- also in declarative-config
    trace-compactor-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml    <- repo only
    trace-flusher-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml      <- also in declarative-config
    trace-syncer-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml       <- repo only

ArgoCD syncs declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, not this repo's .argo/,
so the three repo-only templates have never been applied to the cluster. Analytics,
compactor and syncer therefore have no CI at all: nothing builds or publishes them.

One bead rather than three: the three files land in one directory in one
declarative-config commit, and splitting would put three concurrent workers into a
repo with a documented history-rewrite hazard.

## Done when
    for t in analytics compactor syncer; do
      ls ~/declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/trace-$t-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml
    done
-> all three listed

    kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig get workflowtemplates -n argo-workflows \
      | grep -E 'trace-(analytics|compactor|syncer)-ci'
-> all three present in the cluster
issue.title: Sync the repo-only Argo CI templates into declarative-config

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phases 5/8 ship scheduled analytics and compaction.

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
    grep -h '^kind:' k8s/*.yaml | sort | uniq -c
      2 kind: CronJob      <-- prohibited
      6 kind: Deployment
      ...

k8s/analytics-cronjob.yaml and k8s/compactor-cronjob.yaml are `kind: CronJob`, which
CLAUDE.md prohibits outright: "Never write `kind: Job` or `kind: CronJob`. ArgoCD
cannot manage them idempotently and their pods are not ArgoCD-owned, so they are never
pruned and hold resource reservations forever."

Mitigating fact, not an excuse: neither file is in declarative-config, so neither is
deployed today -- this is a latent violation waiting for whoever wires the deployment.

Sanctioned replacement per the same rule: a Deployment with an internal scheduling
loop, or an Argo WorkflowTemplate for genuinely one-shot work.

## Done when
    grep -rl 'kind: CronJob' k8s/
-> prints nothing

    grep -h '^kind:' k8s/*.yaml | sort | uniq -c
-> shows no Job or CronJob, and the scheduled analytics/compaction behaviour is
   carried by a Deployment with an internal loop (or an Argo WorkflowTemplate)
issue.title: Replace the two CronJob manifests banned by the org rules
